result.rationale: The diff shows `const calendarId = externalCalendarId ? externalCalendarId : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId;` in GoogleCalendarService.deleteEvent. When `externalCalendarId` is falsy, the find predicate compares `cal.externalId === undefined` (a falsy value), so it can never match and `calendarId` becomes undefined — whereas the old code fell back to `event.destinationCalendar?.externalId`. The dead-fallback mechanism is verifiable directly from the diff; the precise downstream failure mode (API error vs. silent default) is plausible

judged_text: Same dead fallback in deleteEvent: when externalCalendarId is falsy the find predicate `cal.externalId === externalCalendarId` never matches, so calendarId is undefined instead of the old `event.destinationCalendar?.externalId`. Cancelling affected bookings no longer deletes the Google Calendar event (the API call fails), leaving orphaned events on the host's calendar after every cancellation — a permanent data-integrity leak for legacy bookings handled by the no-credentialId path in handleCancelBooking.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`, `deleteEvent` now computes `calendarId` as `externalCalendarId ? externalCalendarId : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId;`. When `externalCalendarId` is falsy (e.g. `null`/`undefined`), the `find` predicate compares against that falsy value and will not match any real `cal.externalId`, so the fallback yields `undefined` instead of the prior `event.destinationCalendar?.externalId`. This is a concrete regression visible in the diff and can cause deletes to target an undefined/primary calendar rather than the intended destination calendar (or fail), leaving events undeleted.
